questions.question: Which was the only nationalised bank in India before 1969?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**SBI**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **State Bank of India (SBI)** was the only nationalized commercial bank in India before the major nationalization drive of **1969**. It was nationalized on **1 July 1955**.
 
• The nationalization was carried out under the **State Bank of India Act, 1955**, which followed the recommendations of the **All India Rural Credit Survey Committee (1954)**.
 
• Prior to its nationalization, it was known as the **Imperial Bank of India**, which had been created in **1921** by amalgamating the three presidency banks: the **Bank of Bengal (1806)**, the **Bank of Bombay (1840)**, and the **Bank of Madras (1843)**.
 
• While the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** was nationalized earlier in **1949**, it serves as the **central bank** and regulator of the country, whereas **SBI** functioned as the sole nationalized **commercial bank** during the **1955-1969** period.
 
• This move was intended to extend banking facilities to rural and semi-urban areas and to provide credit for agricultural and industrial development, fulfilling the government's social and economic objectives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nationalization of 14 Banks (1969):**

 
 
• On **19 July 1969**, the Government of India, led by Prime Minister **Indira Gandhi**, nationalized **14 major commercial banks**.
 
• These banks were selected because they held deposits exceeding **50 crore**.
 
• The list included **Central Bank of India**, **Bank of Baroda**, **Allahabad Bank**, Punjab National Bank, Canara Bank, and others.
 
 
 
• **Nationalization of 6 Banks (1980):**
 
 
• A second phase of nationalization occurred on **15 April 1980**, involving **6 more banks**.
 
• These banks were nationalized as their demand and time liabilities exceeded **200 crore**.
 
 
 
• **State Bank of India (SBI) Today:**
 
 
• It is currently the **largest public sector bank** in India and a **Fortune 500** company.
 
• Headquartered in **Mumbai**, it has over **22,000 branches** and a significant international presence.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Associate Banks of SBI:** In **1959**, the **State Bank of India (Subsidiary Banks) Act** was passed, which enabled SBI to take over eight state-associated banks as its subsidiaries (later known as Associate Banks).
 
• **SBI Merger (2017):** In a landmark move on **1 April 2017**, five associate banks (State Bank of Bikaner and Jaipur, State Bank of Hyderabad, State Bank of Mysore, State Bank of Patiala, and State Bank of Travancore) and the **Bharatiya Mahila Bank** were merged into the **State Bank of India**.
 
• **Banking Regulation:** All nationalized banks, including SBI, are regulated under the **Banking Regulation Act, 1949**, alongside the specific acts under which they were established.
 
• **Allahabad Bank:** It was the oldest joint-stock bank in India, established in **1865**, but it was a **private entity** until its nationalization in **1969**. It was recently merged into the **Indian Bank** in **2020**.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding Second five year plan of India?

I. The targeted growth rate was 8.6 percent.

II. Rapid industrialisation was the objective of this plan.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Second Five-Year Plan** of India was implemented between the years **1956 and 1961**.
 
• This plan was based on the **Mahalanobis model**, developed by the famous Indian statistician **Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis** in **1953**.
 
• The **targeted growth rate** for the **Second Five-Year Plan** was **4.5 percent**, but the actual growth achieved was approximately **4.27 percent**. The figure of **8.6 percent** mentioned in the statement is incorrect as it does not align with the historical economic targets of this specific period. ***Hence, statement I is incorrect.***
 
• The primary objective of the **Second Five-Year Plan** was **rapid industrialisation** with a particular emphasis on the development of **basic and heavy industries**.
 
• It aimed to increase the **public sector's** role in the economy to shift the workforce from agriculture to industry. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***
 
• The plan also focused on **increasing national income** by **25 percent** to raise the standard of living of the Indian population.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Only II.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Focus on Heavy Industries:**

 
 
• During the **Second Five-Year Plan**, the Indian government established several **hydroelectric power projects** and five **steel plants**.
 
• Steel plants at **Bhilai** (with **USSR** assistance), **Durgapur** (with **UK** assistance), and **Rourkela** (with **West German** assistance) were initiated during this period.
 
• The **Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956** was adopted, which paved the way for the **public sector** to dominate the industrial landscape.
 
 
 
• **Economic Context:**
 
 
• The plan faced a **foreign exchange crisis** due to the massive import of **capital goods** required for **industrialisation**.
 
• The **Atomic Energy Commission** was established in **1958** with **Homi J. Bhabha** as the first chairman.
 
• The **Tata Institute of Fundamental Research** was also expanded during this timeframe to bolster scientific research.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with First Plan:**

 
 
• While the **First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956)** was based on the **Harrod-Domar model** and focused primarily on **agriculture**, the second plan shifted the focus entirely toward **industry**.
 
• The **target growth** of the first plan was **2.1 percent**, and it successfully achieved **3.6 percent**.
 
 
 
• **Key Achievements of the Second Plan:**
 
 
• **1956:** Industrial Policy Resolution (IPR) defined the **Socialist Pattern of Society**.
 
• **Railway lines** were expanded, and the **Chittaranjan Locomotive Works** was strengthened.
 
• The **Khadi and Village Industries Commission** was established to promote rural employment alongside large-scale industries.

questions.question:
In India, which of the following statement is correct regarding Industrial Policy Resolution 1956?

I. It classified industries into three categories.

II. The first category comprised industries were exclusively reserved for private players.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956** (IPR 1956) was a landmark policy adopted by the **Government of India** to shape the industrial growth of the country. It was introduced to fulfill the objectives of the **Second Five-Year Plan**, which was based on the **Mahalanobis Model**.
 
• One of the core features of the **IPR 1956** was the classification of industries into **three distinct categories** to define the roles of the **public** and **private sectors**. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• The **first category** (Schedule A) comprised industries that were **exclusively reserved for the State**. Private players were not permitted to start new units in these sectors; they were under the complete ownership of the **government**. ***Hence, statement II is incorrect.***
 
• The policy aimed to achieve a **socialistic pattern of society**, where the **State** would lead the industrialization process, particularly in **heavy** and **basic industries**.
 
• Under this resolution, the **private sector** was kept under state control through a system of **industrial licensing**, ensuring that industrial development aligned with the national priorities set by the **Planning Commission**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of Industries in IPR 1956:**

 
 
• **Schedule A:** This included **17 industries** such as **arms and ammunition**, **atomic energy**, **iron and steel**, **heavy plant and machinery**, **railways**, and **shipbuilding**. These were the sole responsibility of the **Central Government**.
 
• **Schedule B:** This category consisted of **12 industries** which were to be progressively **State-owned**, but where the **private sector** was expected to supplement the efforts of the State. Examples include **fertilizers**, **synthetic rubber**, and **chemical pulp**.
 
• **Schedule C:** All the remaining industries fell into this category and were left open to the **private sector**. However, their operation was subject to the provisions of the **Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951**.
 
 
 
• **Small-Scale Industries (SSI):**
 
 
• The **IPR 1956** emphasized the importance of **Small-scale industries** and **village industries** for generating **employment** and ensuring a fair distribution of national income.
 
• In **1955**, the **Karve Committee** (Village and Small-scale Industries Committee) noted the possibility of using small industries for promoting **rural development**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Industrial Licensing:** To promote **regional equality**, the **government** used **licensing** as a tool. It was easier to obtain a license if the **industrial unit** was established in an **economically backward area**. This was intended to reduce regional disparities.
 
• **Tax Benefits:** Industries set up in backward regions were given **tax concessions** and **subsidies** on **electricity** and **water** to encourage **decentralized industrial growth**.
 
• **Economic Constitution:** The **Industrial Policy Resolution 1956** is often referred to as the **"Economic Constitution of India"** because it laid down the basic framework for India's **mixed economy** for several decades until the **New Economic Policy** of **1991**.

questions.question: Who became the ruler of the Maurya Empire after Chandragupta Maurya around 297 BC?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bindusara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bindusara** was the second emperor of the **Maurya Empire** and the son of its founder, **Chandragupta Maurya**. He ascended the throne in approximately **297 BC** after his father abdicated to follow **Jainism**.
 
• He is known by various names in historical texts, including **Amitraghata** (Slayer of Enemies) in Sanskrit and **Amitrochates** in Greek records, signifying his successful preservation and slight expansion of the empire.
 
• Under his reign, the **Maurya Empire** maintained its vast territories stretching from the **North-West** (modern-day Afghanistan) to the **Deccan** region in the south.
 
• **Bindusara** was the father of **Ashoka the Great**, who eventually became the third and most famous Mauryan ruler.
 
• Unlike his father, who turned to **Jainism**, or his son, who embraced **Buddhism**, **Bindusara** was a patron of the **Ajivika** sect, a fatalistic school of philosophy. ***Hence, the correct answer is Bindusara.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ashoka (Option 1):**

 
 
• He was the son of **Bindusara** and succeeded him in **268 BC** after a four-year succession conflict.
 
• He is renowned for the **Kalinga War** in **261 BC**, which led him to renounce violence and promote **Dhamma** through his **Edicts**. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect as he came after Bindusara.*
 
 
 
• **Dhanananda (Option 3):**
 
 
• He was the last ruler of the **Nanda Dynasty** who was overthrown by **Chandragupta Maurya** with the assistance of **Chanakya**.
 
• His rule ended around **322-321 BC**, marking the beginning of the Mauryan era. *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect as he preceded the Maurya Empire.*
 
 
 
• **Bimbisara (Option 4):**
 
 
• He was the ruler of the **Haryanka Dynasty** of **Magadha**, ruling much earlier from approximately **544 BC to 492 BC**.
 
• He was a contemporary of **Gautama Buddha** and used matrimonial alliances to strengthen **Magadha**. *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect as he belonged to a different dynasty and era.*
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Administrative Continuity:** During **Bindusara's** reign, the famous strategist **Chanakya** (Kautilya) continued to serve as the prime minister, ensuring political stability across the empire.
 
• **Foreign Diplomacy:** **Bindusara** maintained friendly relations with the **Hellenistic** kingdoms. He communicated with the **Seleucid** king **Antiochus I Soter**, requesting sweet wine, dried figs, and a philosopher (sophist).
 
• **Geography:** The capital of the empire during his reign remained **Pataliputra** (modern-day Patna, Bihar), which was one of the largest cities in the world at that time.
 
• **Succession:** Historians suggest that **Bindusara** died around **273 BC**, leading to a war of succession among his sons, from which **Ashoka** emerged victorious.

questions.question:
Which of the following uses a parasitic nutritive strategy?

I. Cuscuta

II. Ticks
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Parasitic nutrition** is a type of **heterotrophic nutrition** in which an organism, known as the **parasite**, lives on or inside the body of another living organism, called the **host**, and derives its nourishment from it without killing it immediately.
 
• **Cuscuta** (commonly known as **Amarbel**) is a yellow, tubular plant that lacks **chlorophyll**. Because it cannot perform **photosynthesis**, it climbs onto other plants and uses specialized structures called **haustoria** to suck nutrients and water from the host plant's **vascular system**. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• **Ticks** are small, blood-sucking **arachnids** that act as **ectoparasites**. They attach themselves to the skin of **mammals**, **birds**, or **reptiles** to feed on their **blood**, which provides the necessary protein and nutrients for their **life cycle** and **reproduction**. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***
 
• Both **Cuscuta** and **Ticks** are classic examples of organisms that rely on a **parasitic strategy**, as they benefit at the expense of the **host organism**, often causing harm or **nutritional deficiency** to the host.
 
• ***Therefore, the correct answer is Both I and II.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of Parasites**:

 
 
• **Ectoparasites**: These organisms live on the **external surface** of the host. Examples include **lice**, **ticks**, **mites**, and **leeches**.
 
• **Endoparasites**: These organisms live **inside the host's body**, often in organs like the **intestines** or **liver**. Examples include **tapeworms**, **hookworms**, and **Plasmodium** (the parasite that causes **malaria**).
 
 
 
• **Modes of Heterotrophic Nutrition**:
 
 
• **Saprotrophic Nutrition**: Organisms like **fungi** and certain **bacteria** feed on **dead and decaying organic matter** by secreting **digestive enzymes** externally.
 
• **Holozoic Nutrition**: Organisms like **humans**, **dogs**, and **Amoeba** ingest **solid food**, which is then broken down and **digested** inside the body.
 
• **Parasitic Nutrition**: As discussed, this involves deriving food from a **living host** (e.g., **Liver fluke**, **Cuscuta**).
 
 
 
• **Parasitic Plants**:
 
 
• While **Cuscuta** is a **total parasite**, some plants are **partial parasites**. For example, **Mistletoe** has **green leaves** and can perform **photosynthesis** but relies on the host for **water and minerals**.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Hosts**:
 
 
• Parasites often cause **diseases**, reduced **growth rates**, or even **sterility** in their hosts. In **agriculture**, **Cuscuta** is considered a major **weed** because it significantly reduces **crop yields**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Biological Interaction**: Parasitism is a **symbiotic relationship** where one species (the parasite) **benefits (+ )** and the other (the host) is **harmed (- )**.
 
• **Adaptations**: Parasites often evolve specific **adaptations**, such as the loss of **unnecessary sense organs**, the presence of **adhesive organs** (suckers or hooks), and **high reproductive capacity** to ensure survival.
 
• **Host Specificity**: Many parasites are **host-specific**, meaning they can only survive on a **particular species** of host, evolving alongside them over **millions of years**.

questions.question: The term 'Chalcolithic' literally means _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Copper and Stone Age**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **Chalcolithic** is derived from the **Greek** words **'Khalkos'**, which means **copper**, and **'Lithos'**, which means **stone**.
 
• This era represents a significant phase in human prehistory that marks the transition between the **Neolithic** (New Stone Age) and the **Bronze Age**.
 
• During this period, humans discovered the use of **metal** for the first time, specifically **copper**, while still relying heavily on **lithic** (stone) technology for daily tools and weapons.
 
• The **Chalcolithic** period is also referred to as the **Eneolithic** or **Aeneolithic** age in various archaeological contexts globally.
 
• In the **Indian subcontinent**, this period roughly dates from **2100 BCE** to **700 BCE**, although different regional cultures emerged at different times. ***Hence, the correct answer is Copper and Stone Age.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Major Chalcolithic Cultures in India:**

 
 
• The **Ahar-Banas culture** (approx. **2100–1500 BCE**) flourished in the **Banas river valley** in **Rajasthan**, known for sites like **Ahar** and **Gilund**.
 
• The **Kayatha culture** (approx. **2450–1700 BCE**) was located in **Madhya Pradesh** on the banks of the **Chhoti Sarila river**.
 
• The **Malwa culture** (approx. **1700–1200 BCE**) was spread across **Central India** and **Maharashtra**, with prominent sites such as **Navdatoli** and **Eran**.
 
• The **Jorwe culture** (approx. **1400–700 BCE**) was the most extensive **Chalcolithic** culture in **Maharashtra**, featuring large settlements like **Daimabad** and **Inamgaon**.
 
 
 
• **Economic and Social Features:**
 
 
• People of this age were primarily **farmers** and **herders**. They cultivated crops like **wheat**, **barley**, **rice**, **lentils**, and **black gram**.
 
• They domesticated animals such as **cows**, **sheep**, **goats**, **pigs**, and **buffaloes**, and were known to practice hunting and fishing.
 
• The **Chalcolithic** people lived in **mud-brick** or **wattle-and-daub** houses. Rectangular or circular hut structures have been excavated at several sites.
 
• They were pioneers in **copper smelting** and metalworking, creating artifacts like **axes**, **knives**, **chisels**, and **bangles**.
 
 
 
• **Pottery and Art:**
 
 
• One of the most distinctive features of this age is the **Black-and-Red ware** pottery, which was often painted with white linear designs.
 
• The **Malwa pottery** is considered the richest among the **Chalcolithic** ceramics due to its elaborate designs and surface treatment.
 
• Terracotta figurines of the **Mother Goddess** and the **Bull** suggest early religious practices and fertility cults.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Limitations of the Period:** While they used **copper**, the metal was generally soft and scarce, meaning it could not replace **stone** for heavy-duty tasks; thus, the dual use of **copper and stone** remained necessary.
 
• **Burial Practices:** In **Maharashtra**, people buried their dead in an **urn** under the floor of their houses in a **north-to-south** direction, while in **South India**, the **east-to-west** orientation was preferred.
 
• **Urbanization:** Unlike the **Harappan Civilization** (which was a **Bronze Age** urban culture), most **Chalcolithic** settlements in **India** remained **rural** in character, although sites like **Daimabad** and **Inamgaon** reached a near-urban stage.

questions.question: The traditional folk dance 'Kunbi' belongs to which of the following regions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Kunbi** dance is a traditional folk dance belonging to the state of **Goa**, performed by the **Kunbi community**, who are the **original settlers** or **tribal inhabitants** of the **Konkan** region.
 
• It is predominantly a **women-led** dance form, characterized by its **simple yet fast-paced** movements that reflect the **social life** and **cultural traditions** of the tribe.
 
• Unlike many other folk dances that center around **religious deities**, the **Kunbi dance** is unique as it primarily focuses on **social themes**, though it is often performed during festivals like **Shigmo** and other social gatherings.
 
• The performers wear a traditional **Kunbi saree**, which is usually **red or checkered**, knotted on the **right shoulder** and worn slightly above the **ankles** to allow for rhythmic footwork.
 
• The dance is accompanied by the rhythmic beats of traditional musical instruments, most notably the **Ghumat** (an earthen pot drum) and the **Shamel**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Goa**:

 
 
• Other prominent folk dances of **Goa** include **Fugdi**, **Dhalo**, **Dekhni**, **Corridinho**, and **Mando**.
 
• The **Mando** is a beautiful blend of **Indian** and **Western** musical influences, reflecting the **Portuguese** legacy in the **coastal state**.
 
 
 
• **Assam**:
 
 
• This **North-Eastern** state is famous for the **Bihu** dance, performed during the **Rongali Bihu** festival to celebrate the **harvest**.
 
• **Sattriya**, which originated in the **15th century**, is the **classical dance** form of **Assam**, introduced by the saint **Mahapurusha Sankaradeva**.
 
 
 
• **Mizoram**:
 
 
• The **Cheraw** dance, also known as the **Bamboo Dance**, is the most iconic folk dance of **Mizoram**, involving the rhythmic clapping of **bamboo staves**.
 
• Other dances like **Khuallam** and **Chheihlam** are performed during community feasts and celebrations.
 
 
 
• **Gujarat**:
 
 
• **Garba** and **Dandiya Raas** are the world-renowned folk dances of **Gujarat**, performed with great enthusiasm during the **nine nights** of the **Navratri** festival.
 
• The **Tippani** dance is another unique form, traditionally performed by **women laborers** in the **Saurashtra** region using **long sticks** to beat the floor.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Kunbi saree**, which is the attire for this dance, has seen a modern revival and is considered a symbol of **Goan heritage**. It is made of **sturdy cotton** to withstand **agricultural work**.
 
• The **Kunbi community** is traditionally an **agrarian** society, and their dance movements often mimic the **sowing** and **harvesting** processes.
 
• Despite over **450 years** of **Portuguese rule** in **Goa**, the **Kunbi dance** has largely retained its **indigenous tribal** purity and **traditional rhythm**.
 
• Efforts by the **Government of Goa** and **cultural organizations** have helped in promoting the **Kunbi folk dance** at national platforms like the **Republic Day Parade** in **New Delhi**.

questions.question: Rathawa' dance, associated with the Rathwa tribe, is a traditional folk dance of which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gujarat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Rathawa** dance is a vibrant folk dance associated with the **Rathwa** tribe, who primarily reside in the state of **Gujarat**.
 
• This dance is most famously performed during the **Holi** festival, which the tribe refers to as **Gher** or **Kawant**, marking the celebration of spring and harvest.
 
• The performers are mainly found in the tribal-dominated districts of **Chhota Udepur**, **Panchmahal**, and parts of **Vadodara** in **Gujarat**.
 
• Male dancers typically wear attractive headgears adorned with **Peacock feathers** and colorful costumes that reflect their tribal identity.
 
• The performance is accompanied by traditional musical instruments such as the **Dhol** (drum), **Piho** (flute), **Dobra**, and **Kunda**, which dictate the high-energy rhythm of the dance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tribal Heritage of Gujarat:**

 
 
• The **Rathwa** community is recognized as a **Scheduled Tribe** (ST) under the Constitution of India in the state of **Gujarat**.
 
• Apart from their dance, they are globally renowned for **Pithora** paintings, which are sacred wall murals painted on the walls of their houses to invoke divine blessings.
 
• The **Kavant Fair** (Kavant no Melo) is a major cultural event held after **Holi** where thousands of **Rathwa** tribespeople gather to showcase their traditional art and dance.
 
 
 
• **Other Folk Dances of Gujarat:**
 
 
• **Garba**: A world-famous dance performed during the nine nights of **Navratri**, involving circular movements around a lamp or Goddess Durga.
 
• **Dandiya Raas**: A rhythmic dance performed with wooden sticks, depicting the mock fight between the Goddess and **Mahishasura**.
 
• **Bhavai**: A popular folk drama or theatre form of **Western India**, especially **Gujarat**, involving balance and acrobatic skills.
 
• **Tippani**: A dance performed by women workers, originating from the **Chorwad** region, involving the beating of the floor with sticks.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Rathwa ni Gher** dance involves performers forming large circles, and they often paint their bodies with **natural dyes** and **white clay** to create patterns resembling leopards or tigers.
 
• The dancers sometimes create **human pyramids** during the festivities, demonstrating great physical strength and coordination.
 
• While **Gujarat** is the primary home, some members of the **Rathwa** tribe also reside in the bordering areas of **Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• The state of **Gujarat** was established on **May 1, 1960**, following the **Bombay Reorganisation Act**, and it remains a hub for diverse tribal cultures including the **Bhils**, **Siddhis**, and **Rathwas**.

questions.question: Some plants like the pea plant climb up other plants or fences by means of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tendrils**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tendrils** are specialized, thread-like structures that are sensitive to touch. They are modified **stems, leaves, or even petioles** used by climbing plants for support.
 
• In the case of the **pea plant** (**Pisum sativum**), the **terminal leaflets** of the compound leaf are modified into **tendrils**. These structures help the plant, which has a **weak stem**, to climb up supports like **fences, sticks, or other plants**.
 
• When a **tendril** comes into contact with any support, the side of the tendril in contact with the object does not grow as rapidly as the side away from the object. This **differential growth** causes the tendril to **coil** around the support.
 
• The growth movement of a plant part in response to **touch** is known as **thigmotropism**. This is the physiological principle that allows climbing plants to anchor themselves effectively.
 
• The primary function of these structures is to allow **weak-stemmed plants** to ascend toward **sunlight**, which is essential for the process of **photosynthesis**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Thorns**: These are hard, pointed, and sharp structures which are modifications of the **axillary buds** of the **stem**. They are commonly found in plants like **Citrus** and **Bougainvillea**. Their main function is **protection** from browsing animals and to reduce **transpiration** in some desert plants.
 
• **Root hair**: These are tiny, unicellular outgrowths of the **root epidermis** (epiblema) found in the **region of maturation**. They play a critical role in increasing the surface area for the **absorption of water and minerals** from the soil through the process of **osmosis**.
 
• **Cell sap**: This is the fluid located inside the **vacuole** of a plant cell. It is a dilute solution of **minerals, salts, sugars, and amino acids**. It serves to maintain **turgor pressure** within the cell, providing mechanical strength and support to non-woody plant parts, but it is not an organ for climbing.
 
• **Modified Stems vs. Modified Leaves**: It is important to note that while tendrils in **peas** are modified **leaves**, in other plants like **grapes (Vitis vinifera)**, the tendrils are modified **stems**. Both serve the same climbing function, illustrating **homoplasy** or convergent evolution.
 
• **Other Climbing Mechanisms**: Some plants use **climbing roots** (e.g., **Money plant** or **Piper betle**) which arise from the nodes and internodes to attach the plant to a vertical surface. Others, known as **twiners**, simply wrap their entire main stem around a support.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Thigmotropism**: A directional growth movement that occurs as a mechanosensory response to a **touch stimulus**. This is highly developed in **tendrils**.
 
• **Circumnutation**: Before reaching a support, tendrils often perform a sweeping circular motion in the air to increase the probability of encountering a **physical object** to climb.
 
• **Anatomy**: The coiling of the tendril is often accompanied by the formation of **sclerenchyma** (strengthening tissue), which provides the permanent **mechanical strength** needed to hold the weight of the plant once the coil is established.

questions.question: The Kumbh Mela at Prayagraj is held once every how many years?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**12 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Kumbh Mela** is a major spiritual gathering in **Hinduism** and is considered the largest peaceful congregation of pilgrims in the world.
 
• In **Prayagraj**, the **Purna Kumbh Mela** is held every **12 years** at the **Triveni Sangam**, which is the confluence of the rivers **Ganga**, **Yamuna**, and the mythical **Saraswati**.
 
• The timing of the festival is determined by the **Vikram Samvat** calendar and the **astronomical positions** of **Jupiter** (Brihaspati), the **Sun**, and the **Moon**.
 
• According to tradition, the mela is held when **Jupiter** enters **Taurus** (Vrishabha Rashi) and the **Sun** and **Moon** are in **Capricorn** (Makara Rashi) during the Hindu month of **Magha**.
 
• UNESCO inscribed the **Kumbh Mela** on the **Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity** in **December 2017**, recognizing its cultural and spiritual significance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Four Sacred Locations**: The Kumbh Mela rotates among four holy sites across **India**: **Prayagraj** (Uttar Pradesh), **Haridwar** (Uttarakhand), **Nashik** (Maharashtra), and **Ujjain** (Madhya Pradesh).

 
 
• **Haridwar**: Held on the banks of the **Ganga** when Jupiter is in Aquarius and the Sun is in Aries.
 
• **Nashik**: Held on the banks of the **Godavari** when Jupiter and the Sun are in Leo.
 
• **Ujjain**: Held on the banks of the **Shipra** when Jupiter is in Leo and the Sun is in Aries (often called **Simhastha Kumbh**).
 
 
 
• **Cycle and Types**:
 
 
• **Ardh Kumbh Mela**: Meaning "Half Kumbh," it is held every **6 years** at only two locations: **Haridwar** and **Prayagraj**.
 
• **Purna Kumbh Mela**: The "Full Kumbh" occurs every **12 years** at all four locations.
 
• **Maha Kumbh Mela**: This occurs after **12 cycles** of the Purna Kumbh, which means once every **144 years**, and is specifically held at **Prayagraj**.
 
 
 
• **Mythological Origin**: The origin of the festival is linked to the **Samudra Manthan** (churning of the cosmic ocean). It is believed that drops of **Amrita** (the nectar of immortality) fell from a **Kumbh** (pot) at the four locations where the mela is now celebrated.
 
• **Key Rituals**: The most significant ritual is the **Shahi Snan** (Royal Bath), where **Sadhus** (holy men) from various **Akharas** lead the pilgrims into the water to achieve **Moksha** (liberation from the cycle of birth and death).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The last **Ardh Kumbh** at **Prayagraj** took place in **2019**, while the previous **Purna Kumbh** was held in **2013**.
 
• The next **Maha Kumbh** is scheduled to be held at **Prayagraj** in the year **2025**, starting on **Makar Sankranti**.
 
• During the event, temporary cities called **Kumbh Nagari** are established to accommodate millions of pilgrims, showcasing massive **administrative** and **logistical** management by the government.
 
• The festival also serves as a platform for **religious discourses**, **Vedic chanting**, and the gathering of various sects like the **Naga Sadhus**, **Kalpavasis**, and **Urdhwavahurs**.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of festival – religion associated with is correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Barah Wafat – Islam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahavir Jayanti** is incorrectly paired with Buddhism. It is actually the most important religious festival for the **Jain community**. It celebrates the birth anniversary of **Lord Mahavira**, who was the **24th and last Tirthankara** of **Jainism**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Guru Nanak Jayanti**, also known as **Gurpurab**, is incorrectly paired with Christianity. This festival marks the birth anniversary of **Guru Nanak Dev**, the **first Guru** and the **founder of Sikhism**. It is observed on the full moon day of the month of **Kartik**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Buddha Jayanti**, also known as **Buddha Purnima** or **Vesak**, is incorrectly paired with Jainism. This day commemorates the birth, enlightenment (**Nirvana**), and death (**Parinirvana**) of **Gautama Buddha**, the **founder of Buddhism**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Barah Wafat** is correctly paired with **Islam**. Also known as **Eid-e-Milad** or **Mawlid**, it is observed by **Muslims** to commemorate the birth and the death anniversary of **Prophet Muhammad**. It falls in the **third month** of the **Islamic calendar**, known as **Rabi-ul-Awwal**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Barah Wafat – Islam.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jainism and Mahavir Jayanti:**

 
 
• **Lord Mahavira** was born in the **6th century BC** at **Kundagrama** in **Bihar**.
 
• The festival is celebrated in the month of **Chaitra** (March/April).
 
• Key rituals include **Abhisheka** (ceremonial bath) of the idol and organizing **charitable acts** and **processions** (Rath Yatra) to spread the message of **Ahimsa** (non-violence).
 
 
 
• **Sikhism and Guru Nanak Jayanti:**
 
 
• **Guru Nanak Dev** was born in **1469** at **Nankana Sahib** (now in Pakistan).
 
• The celebration involves **Akhand Path** (48-hour non-stop reading of **Guru Granth Sahib**) and **Nagar Kirtan**.
 
• The **Langar** (community kitchen) is a central part of the celebration, emphasizing **equality** and **service**.
 
 
 
• **Buddhism and Buddha Jayanti:**
 
 
• **Gautama Buddha** (born as **Siddhartha Gautama**) was born in **Lumbini**, Nepal, around **563 BC**.
 
• Significant sites for this festival include **Bodh Gaya** (where he attained enlightenment), **Sarnath** (first sermon), and **Kushinagar** (death).
 
• Devotees visit **Viharas** (monasteries), offer prayers, and emphasize the **Eightfold Path**.
 
 
 
• **Islam and Barah Wafat:**
 
 
• The term **'Barah'** stands for the **twelve days** of the Prophet's sickness before his death.
 
• The festival is marked by **discourses** (Milad Mehfils) on the life and **teachings** of the **Prophet Muhammad**.
 
• It is a day of **solemn reflection** as well as **rejoicing**, depending on the specific cultural traditions within different **Islamic sects**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Luni-Solar Calendars:** Most Indian religious festivals like **Mahavir Jayanti**, **Guru Nanak Jayanti**, and **Buddha Purnima** are calculated based on the **Lunar cycle**, which is why their dates on the **Gregorian calendar** change every year.
 
• **Islamic Calendar:** The **Hijri calendar** used for **Barah Wafat** is purely **lunar** and consists of **354 or 355 days**, causing Islamic festivals to move backward through the seasons every year.
 
• **Cultural Impact:** These festivals reflect the **secular fabric** of India, where diverse religious events are celebrated with state-recognized **public holidays** and communal harmony.

questions.question: What is the frictional force exerted by fluids known as?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Drag**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Drag** is the specific term used in **physics** and **fluid dynamics** to describe the **frictional force** exerted by **fluids** (which include both **liquids** and **gases**) on any object moving through them.
 
• The magnitude of **fluid friction** or **drag** depends on the **speed** of the object relative to the fluid; typically, as the **velocity** increases, the resistive force also increases. ***Hence, the correct answer is Drag.***
 
• Another critical factor determining **drag** is the **shape** of the object. Objects that are **streamlined**, such as **aeroplanes**, **submarines**, and **birds**, are designed to minimize this **frictional force** and reduce **energy loss**.
 
• **Fluid friction** is also influenced by the **nature of the fluid**, specifically its **viscosity**. A highly viscous fluid like **honey** or **glycerin** will exert a much greater **drag** than a less viscous fluid like **water** or **air**.
 
• When an object moves through a **fluid**, it must overcome the **resistance** offered by the fluid particles, which results in the conversion of some **kinetic energy** into **heat energy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lift:**

 
 
• **Lift** is a mechanical force generated by a solid object moving through a **fluid**. It acts **perpendicular** to the direction of the flow.
 
• In **aviation**, **lift** is what allows an **aircraft** to overcome **gravity** and stay in the air, usually explained by **Bernoulli's Principle** and **Newton's Third Law of Motion**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect in the context of being the name for frictional force.***
 
 
 
• **Pressure:**
 
 
• **Pressure** is defined as the **force** acting **perpendicularly** on a unit **area** of a surface.
 
• In **fluid mechanics**, it is measured in **Pascals (Pa)**. While fluids exert pressure, it is a scalar quantity and distinct from the resistive frictional force known as **drag**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Load:**
 
 
• A **load** generally refers to the **weight** or the **external force** applied to a structure or component.
 
• In **engineering**, it describes the **mass** or **force** that a system must support, rather than the internal or external **friction** caused by **fluid flow**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Viscosity:**
 
 
• This is a measure of a **fluid's resistance to deformation** or flow. It is often described as the "thickness" of a liquid.
 
• Internal **viscosity** within the fluid layers contributes significantly to the total **drag** experienced by an object. For instance, **engine oil** is designed with specific **viscosity grades** to manage **friction** in **automotive** parts.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Streamlining:** This refers to the process of shaping an object, such as a **car** or **rocket**, to reduce **air resistance** or **water resistance**. **Nature** provides excellent examples of **streamlining** in **dolphins** and **migratory birds** to conserve energy during **long-distance travel**.
 
• **Air Resistance:** This is a specific type of **drag** that acts on objects as they travel through the **atmosphere**. It is a key factor in the **terminal velocity** of falling objects, such as **parachutists**.
 
• **Fluid Friction and Heat:** Just like **solid friction**, **fluid friction** generates **heat**. This is why **spacecraft** entering the **Earth's atmosphere** at high **speeds** require **heat shields** to protect them from the intense heat generated by **atmospheric drag**.

__
 
• **Priya Hajela** is the author of the debut novel titled **"Ladies' Tailor"**, which was published in **2022** by **HarperCollins India**.

• It narrates Gurdev's struggle to rebuild his life and his ambition to start a high-end clothing boutique, focusing on themes of **resilience**, **entrepreneurship**, and the **trauma of displacement**. ***Hence, the correct option is Priya Hajela.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bapsi Sidhwa**:

 
 
• She is a renowned **Pakistani-American** novelist known for her works focusing on the Parsi community and the Partition.
 
• Her most famous novel is **"Ice Candy Man"** (published as **Cracking India** in the US), which was later adapted into the film **Earth** by Deepa Mehta.
 
 
 
• **Amrita Pritam**:
 
 
• A prominent **Punjabi** poet and novelist, she was the first woman to win the **Sahitya Akademi Award** in **1956**.
 
• Her novel **"Pinjar"** (The Skeleton) is considered one of the most poignant accounts of the suffering of women during the **1947 Partition**.
 
• She was also honored with the **Jnanpith Award** in **1982**.
 
 
 
• **Khushwant Singh**:
 
 
• He was a distinguished Indian author, lawyer, and diplomat, best known for his biting wit and historical chronicles.
 
• His masterpiece, **"Train to Pakistan"**, published in **1956**, remains one of the most essential literary works regarding the human tragedy of the **Partition**.
 
• He also authored the multi-volume **"A History of the Sikhs"** and served as a member of the **Rajya Sabha** from **1980 to 1986**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Partition Literature**:
 
 
• Literature like "Ladies' Tailor" serves as a medium to understand the **socio-political** impact of the creation of **India and Pakistan**.
 
• These stories often highlight the **migration** of millions, the **rehabilitation** efforts in cities like **Delhi**, and the cultural shifts occurring in the **mid-20th century**.

questions.question: Which of the following monuments is located in Delhi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Humayun's Tomb**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Humayun's Tomb** is a magnificent garden-tomb located in **Delhi**, specifically in the **Nizamuddin East** area. It was the first **garden-tomb** built on the **Indian subcontinent** and served as a precursor to the **Taj Mahal** in **Agra**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The monument was commissioned in **1565** by **Empress Bega Begum** (also known as **Haji Begum**), who was the first wife and chief consort of the **Mughal Emperor Humayun**. The construction was completed around **1572**.
 
• It was designed by the renowned **Persian architect** **Mirak Mirza Ghiyas**, who was invited from **Herat**. This brought a distinct **Persian** influence to **Indian** architecture, blending it with local traditions to create the **Mughal** style.
 
• The tomb is situated near the **Yamuna River** and the shrine of the **Sufi saint** **Nizamuddin Auliya**. It was declared a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in **1993** for its outstanding universal value.
 
• The structure is built primarily of **red sandstone** with extensive use of **white marble** for the dome and decorative elements, marking a shift in the building materials used by the **Mughals**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Charminar**:

 
 
• This iconic monument is located in **Hyderabad**, **Telangana**.
 
• It was constructed in **1591** by **Sultan Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah**, the fifth ruler of the **Qutb Shahi dynasty**, to mark the end of a plague in the city. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Victoria Memorial**:
 
 
• This grand marble building is situated in **Kolkata**, **West Bengal**.
 
• Built between **1906** and **1921**, it is dedicated to the memory of **Queen Victoria**. It was designed by **Sir William Emerson** in the **Indo-Saracenic** revivalist style. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Gateway of India**:
 
 
• Located on the waterfront in **Mumbai**, **Maharashtra**, this monument overlooks the **Arabian Sea**.
 
• It was built to commemorate the landing of **King George V** and **Queen Mary** at **Apollo Bunder** during their visit to **India** in **1911**. The structure was completed in **1924**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Architecture and Layout**: **Humayun's Tomb** introduced the **Charbagh** (four-quadrant garden) layout to India. The garden is divided into four main squares by paved walkways and water channels, symbolizing the **Islamic** concept of **Paradise**.
 
• **The Dormitory of the Mughals**: The tomb is often referred to as the "**Dormitory of the Mughals**" because it houses over **150 graves** of various **Mughal** family members and descendants.
 
• **Restoration**: In recent years, the **Aga Khan Trust for Culture** (**AKTC**), in partnership with the **Archaeological Survey of India** (**ASI**), has undertaken extensive restoration work to preserve the monument's historical integrity.
 
• **Other Monuments in Delhi**: The capital city is home to several other historical landmarks, including the **Qutub Minar** (constructed by **Qutb-ud-din Aibak** in **1193**), the **Red Fort** (built by **Shah Jahan** in **1639**), and **India Gate** (built in **1921** as a war memorial).

questions.question: What is the architectural pattern of the Panch Mahal in Fatehpur Sikri based on?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Buddhist Vihara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Panch Mahal** is an elaborate five-story structure located within the **Fatehpur Sikri** complex in **Uttar Pradesh**, built by the **Mughal Emperor Akbar** in the late **16th century**.
 
• The architectural pattern of the **Panch Mahal** is primarily based on the **Buddhist Vihara** (monastery) design, which consists of tiered floors where each subsequent level is smaller than the one below it. ***Hence, the correct answer is Buddhist Vihara.***
 
• It is famously known as the "**Wind Tower**" because of its open-pillared structure, designed specifically to provide relief from the intense heat by allowing the passage of cool breezes.
 
• The building features a total of **176 columns**. The ground floor consists of **84 columns**, the first floor has **56 columns**, the second floor has **20 columns**, the third floor has **12 columns**, and the top floor is a simple **domed chhatri** supported by **4 columns**.
 
• Historically, the **Panch Mahal** was used for entertainment and relaxation by the **Emperor** and the ladies of the royal household (the **Zenana**), as it overlooks the **Pachisi Court**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fatehpur Sikri:** This city was founded by **Akbar** in **1571** and served as the capital of the **Mughal Empire** until **1585**. It is recognized as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.
 
• **Architectural Synthesis:** The architecture of **Fatehpur Sikri** is a brilliant example of **Indo-Islamic** style, blending **Persian**, **Central Asian**, and indigenous **Hindu** and **Jain** architectural elements.
 
• **Buland Darwaza:** Also located in **Fatehpur Sikri**, this massive gateway was built in **1601** to commemorate **Akbar's** victory over **Gujarat**. It is known as the "**Gate of Magnificence**."
 
• **Jodha Bai Palace:** This is one of the largest residential complexes in the city, showcasing heavy influence from **Rajasthani** and **Gujarati** architectural motifs.
 
• **Salim Chishti’s Tomb:** A masterpiece of **Mughal** architecture, this white marble structure was built to honor the **Sufi saint Sheikh Salim Chishti**, who had predicted the birth of **Akbar's** heir, **Salim** (later **Emperor Jahangir**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The choice of a **Buddhist Vihara** layout for a **Mughal** structure signifies **Akbar's** **secular** outlook and his interest in various Indian cultural and religious traditions.
 
• The columns of the **Panch Mahal** are intricately carved and vary in design; some show **floral** and **bell** motifs commonly found in **Hindu temple** architecture, highlighting the **syncretic** nature of **Akbar's** reign.
 
• The entire structure is made of **red sandstone**, which was the hallmark of **Akbari** architecture before the shift toward white marble during the reign of **Shah Jahan**.
 
• The **Panch Mahal** stands adjacent to the **Anup Talao**, a beautiful ornamental pool where legendary musician **Tansen** used to perform.

questions.question: Which of the following group of musical instruments are known as Membranophones?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Avanaddha Vadya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Avanaddha Vadya**, also known as **Membranophones**, refers to a category of musical instruments where sound is produced by the vibration of a **stretched membrane** or skin.
 
• These membranes are usually stretched over a **hollow resonator** made of **wood**, **metal**, or **clay**. The intensity of the sound can be adjusted by tightening or loosening the membrane.
 
• In the context of **Indian Classical Music**, these instruments are primarily utilized for keeping the **tala** or the **rhythmic cycle**. ***Hence, option 3 is correct.***
 
• Common examples of **Avanaddha Vadya** include the **Tabla**, **Mridangam**, **Dholak**, **Kanjira**, **Nagada**, and **Damaru**.
 
• The classification of Indian musical instruments into four groups was first detailed in the ancient treatise **Natya Shastra**, compiled by **Bharata Muni** between **200 BC and 200 AD**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ghan Vadya (Idiophones):**

 
 
• These are **solid instruments** that do not require any tuning before they are played.
 
• Sound is produced by **striking** two pieces of the same material together or by striking the instrument's body with a mallet.
 
• Examples include the **Manjira** (cymbals), **Ghatam** (earth pot), **Jaltarang**, and **Khartal**.
 
 
 
• **Tat Vadya (Chordophones):**
 
 
• This group consists of **stringed instruments** where sound is generated through the vibration of **strings**.
 
• The strings can be **plucked** (like the **Sitar** or **Veena**), **bowed** (like the **Sarangi** or **Violin**), or **struck** (like the **Santoor**).
 
• These instruments are essential for providing the **melody** and **drone** (Tanpura) in Indian music.
 
 
 
• **Sushir Vadya (Aerophones):**
 
 
• These are **wind instruments** where sound is produced by the vibration of an **air column**.
 
• The pitch is generally controlled by opening or closing **finger-holes** on the body of the instrument.
 
• Notable examples include the **Bansuri** (flute), **Shehnai**, **Nadaswaram**, and **Harmonium**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Evolution and Variety:** Many **Avanaddha Vadya** instruments are ancient, such as the **Damaru** associated with **Lord Shiva**. They vary significantly in size and shape across different states of **India**, serving both **folk** and **classical** traditions.
 
• **Construction Materials:** While traditional membranes were made from **animal hide** (like goat or cow skin), modern versions may occasionally use **synthetic materials**, though the authentic resonance of **natural parchment** is preferred in classical performances.
 
• **The Role of Rhythm:** In a typical **Hindustani** or **Carnatic** concert, the **Avanaddha Vadya** player provides the structural framework of the performance by maintaining the **Matras** (beats) and **Vibhagas** (measures).

questions.question: Who is the composer of treatise of music Brihaddesi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Matanga**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Matanga Muni**, a legendary musicologist, is the author of the seminal Sanskrit treatise **Brihaddesi**, composed approximately between the **6th and 9th centuries AD**.
 
• The **Brihaddesi** serves as a vital bridge between the ancient music (**Gandharva**) described by **Bharata Muni** in the **Natya Shastra** and the medieval evolution of Indian classical music.
 
• This work is historically significant for being the first to provide a formal definition of the term **Raga**. **Matanga** defines it as a combination of notes that "colors" or "delights" the minds of listeners.
 
• In this treatise, **Matanga** introduced the concept of **Desi Sangeet** (regional music) and **Marga Sangeet** (classical/celestial music), acknowledging for the first time the importance of folk and regional melodies in the classical tradition.
 
• The text also discusses the **Srutis** (microtones), the **Swaras** (notes), and the **Grama** system (the ancient scale systems of **Shadja-grama** and **Madhyama-grama**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sharangadeva (13th Century)**:

 
 
• He was the author of the **Sangita Ratnakara**, which is arguably the most influential work in the history of Indian musicology.
 
• He served in the court of **King Singhana II** of the **Yadava Dynasty** in **Devagiri** (Maharashtra).
 
• His work is often called the **Saptadhyayi** because it consists of **seven chapters** covering everything from sound production to dance and rhythm.
 
 
 
• **Haripala (14th Century)**:
 
 
• **Haripala**, a king of the **Chaulukya Dynasty** in **Gujarat**, authored the treatise **Sangita Sudhakara**.
 
• He is credited with being one of the first scholars to explicitly categorize Indian music into two distinct traditions: **Hindustani Sangeet** (Northern) and **Carnatic Sangeet** (Southern).
 
 
 
• **Ramamatya (16th Century)**:
 
 
• He was a prominent musicologist in the **Vijayanagara Empire** during the reign of **Aliya Rama Raya**.
 
• He wrote the **Svaramelakalanidhi** around **1550 AD**, which laid the conceptual groundwork for the modern **Mela** (parent scale) system used in **Carnatic music** today.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Definition of Desi**: In **Brihaddesi**, **Matanga** explains that music which is performed by **common people** (women, children, and cowherds) in different **Deshas** (regions) for pleasure is known as **Desi**.
 
• **Evolution of Instruments**: **Matanga** provided detailed descriptions of the **Veena** (stringed instruments) and discussed the **Kinnari Veena**, contributing to the development of instrumental music theory.
 
• **Prabandha**: The treatise contains early descriptions of the **Prabandha** form, which were structured musical compositions that preceded modern forms like **Dhrupad** and **Kriti**.
 
• **Legacy**: While large portions of the original **Brihaddesi** have been lost over **centuries**, the surviving fragments remain the primary source for understanding the transition of Indian music into the **Raga** system.
